final_candidates.decision_summary: W17 is a buried aromatic residue essential for hydrophobic core packing; introducing a charged glutamate residue severely destabilizes fold stability.
Y18 contributes significantly to interior hydrophobic interactions; substituting with aspartate incurs a severe desolvation penalty and disrupts core structure.
F40 is a core phenylalanine residue; inserting a charged glutamate into this hydrophobic environment strongly destabilizes local beta-sheet folding.

stop_reason.detail: Top candidate mutations targeting core hydrophobic stability are established and further internal iterations will not refine the selection.

history.rationale: Substituting the conserved aromatic tryptophan at position 17 with a charged glutamate disrupts core hydrophobic packing and severely destabilizes folding.
W17 is a buried aromatic residue critical for hydrophobic core stability; introducing a charged glutamate strongly disrupts folding.
Introducing a negatively charged aspartate at conserved aromatic position 18 disrupts hydrophobic and aromatic interactions critical for core stability.
Y18 contributes key aromatic and hydrophobic packing; aspartate substitution introduces desolvation penalty and charge mismatch.
Replacing hydrophobic isoleucine at position 10 with charged aspartate introduces strong desolvation penalties in the hydrophobic core.
I10 forms part of the hydrophobic N-terminal strand; charged aspartate causes significant local destabilization.
Substituting hydrophobic leucine at position 11 with glutamate introduces a buried negative charge, destabilizing the protein fold.
L11 is a hydrophobic core leucine; glutamate mutation disrupts core packing and lowers thermo-stability.
Inserting a bulky, positively charged arginine residue at core hydrophobic position 38 causes severe steric hindrance and charge mismatch.
V38 is buried in the interior core; substitution with a bulky charged arginine destabilizes folding.
Replacing aromatic phenylalanine at position 40 with negatively charged glutamate disrupts core hydrophobic collapse and tertiary assembly.
F40 is a conserved core phenylalanine; inserting glutamate destabilizes the local beta-sheet structure.
Replacing tyrosine 34 with charged aspartate disrupts tertiary packing and key hydrophobic interactions required for folding.
Y34 participates in hydrophobic core interactions; polar/charged aspartate mutation penalizes tertiary fold stability.
Introducing a proline at position 33 restricts backbone conformational freedom and disrupts local secondary structure.
Proline introduction at I33 disrupts backbone phi/psi angles within the secondary structure element.
